A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same facial appearance capture method. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplementary sections are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original facial reconstruction and relighting experiments, quantitative comparisons in Table 1, synthetic-data ablations and supplementary failure analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds visibility-ablation scores, a CoRA comparison, geometry-smoothing experiments and additional rendering demonstrations.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same geometry preconditioning, ray-traced diffuse illumination, visibility-modulated split-sum specular rendering and reconstruction losses. The rewritten shading explanation and more explicit sampling notation do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The existing indoor/outdoor facial captures and synthetic Lambertian head dataset remain. v2 adds a one-subject experiment under CoRA's colocated light-camera setup in a dark room, a glossy Happy Buddha rendering example and an explicit novel-view demonstration in the capture environment.

E2.justification: FLARE, NextFace and SunStage remain in the corresponding comparisons. CoRA changes from cited related work to an evaluated comparator in supplementary Figure 18. Table 1 also newly includes Ours (w/o vis); the synthetic ray-tracing versus prefiltered-environment comparison is retained under revised labels.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a geometry-smoothing sweep with lambda_geo values 1, 4, 8, 19 and 64, and a matched-data CoRA comparison on one subject. Existing training settings, skin-region metrics in linear RGB and comparator frame-selection procedures remain unchanged; moving implementation settings to the supplement does not constitute a protocol change.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the diagnostic evaluation with quantitative and real-image relighting ablations of visibility handling (Table 1 and Figure 5), geometry-smoothing sensitivity (Figure 16), and glossy-object and novel-view case studies (Figures 13 and 17). Existing synthetic, diffuse-regularization, geometry-parameterization and failure analyses remain, although the original static specular comparison panel is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report subject/frame-averaged point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed replication, confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests. The added experiments introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds quantitative evidence isolating visibility handling: the new Table 1 row reports PSNR 34.55, MAE 1.79, SSIM 0.96 and LPIPS 0.10 without visibility. All original rows remain unchanged, including Ours at 38.09, 1.18, 0.97 and 0.10. Additional findings cover relighting artifacts, smoothing sensitivity, reported comparable reconstruction to CoRA, glossy-object rendering and novel views. The static comparison in the first row of v1 Figure 6 is removed.

T1.justification: The rendering model, visibility approximation, low-roughness assumption, preconditioning and losses retain their mathematical substance. v2 expands the explanation of existing split-sum integrals and makes half-vector and sampling-density notation explicit. It adds no substantive theoretical result, proof or correction to mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and both versions claim lightweight monocular capture under unconstrained environmental lighting, improved appearance reconstruction and explicit self-occlusion handling. Revised contribution and conclusion wording emphasizes the same visibility-aware shading contribution without materially changing the headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 discusses the smoothing tradeoff between detail preservation and self-intersections, applicability to glossy objects, and boundary artifacts associated with masking and alignment. It also identifies hair and shoulder reconstruction as future work. Existing tracking, lighting and roughness limitations remain, but the qualification that the compared ray-traced and prefiltered results use separately optimized parameters is omitted.

D1.justification: Optimizer settings, resolutions, sampling counts, loss weights, training duration and hardware move from the main text to supplementary Section 8 unchanged. Limited documentation changes include settings for the new sensitivity and CoRA experiments and removal of the explicit statement that diffuse denoising is skipped. These changes do not establish a changed underlying implementation.

R1.justification: v2 expands the single-image reconstruction discussion with MoSAR, Han et al.'s low-cost reflectance model, AvatarMe and Relightify, and adds the Veach–Guibas importance-sampling reference. It more explicitly positions the shading formulation relative to existing split-sum approaches. The expanded LitNeRF bibliography entry represents an already cited work.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the shading explanation, reorganizes Section 4.3 as Evaluations, revises contribution wording and moves implementation details into a dedicated supplementary section. These are focused narrative revisions; the abstract and much of the introduction, comparison discussion, capture description and limitations remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The visual evidence expands through new Figure 5 and supplementary Figures 13 and 16–18. Figure 3 gains zoomed patches, Table 1 gains an ablation row, and v1 Figure 6 becomes a reduced two-row comparison in v2 Figure 7. Several retained figures are relabeled or rearranged, substantially revising the evaluation and supplement layouts.

improvement.justification: The direct quantitative visibility ablation, matched-protocol CoRA comparison and smoothing-sensitivity study improve support for the existing method, while the revised shading explanation and boundary discussion improve clarity. These extend an already substantial evaluation, with many additions remaining qualitative. Some useful ray-tracing comparison context is lost, and stale Figure 7 row references remain, but the net quality gain is positive and limited.
